title: Rabbi Yaakov of Kefar Chitayya

paragraphs: [Chagigah 5b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.5b) relates that Rabbi and Rabbi Chiyya came to a certain place and went to greet a Torah scholar who was blind. He blessed them, and they asked him: “From whom did you hear this?” He told them that he had heard it in a discourse of Rabbi Yaakov of Kefar Chitayya, who used to greet his teacher every day. When he (Rabbi Yaakov) grew old, he was told: “Let the master not trouble himself,” etc.[^1]

notes.text: מאור עינים (‘light of the eyes’) is a euphemism for blindness. The final speaker is unnamed. The Hebrew alternates חיטייה and חיטייא.
